questions.q: What is a Critical Data Element (CDE), per this lesson?
options: A data element whose accuracy, timeliness, or integrity has outsized consequences if it's wrong
Any column that has a non-empty description in the dictionary
Every column in a table with more than ten rows
A column that is never allowed to be NULL
questions.explain: CDE status is a deliberately small, selective subset reserved for data where errors are genuinely expensive, not just inconvenient.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say treating every column as equally critical is a problem?
options: It is functionally the same as treating nothing as critical, since scrutiny gets spread too thin to matter anywhere
It is illegal under every data protection regulation
It makes databases run measurably slower
It requires buying additional storage hardware
questions.explain: Naming a small set of genuinely critical elements lets an organization concentrate real governance effort where it actually matters, instead of diluting it everywhere.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four CDE criteria named in this lesson?
options: Regulatory relevance
Financial materiality
Downstream reach
The column's exact character length in the database
questions.explain: The four criteria are regulatory relevance, financial materiality, decision impact, and downstream reach — a column's character length is a technical dictionary field, not a CDE criterion.

questions.q: In the worked example, why was dbo.Orders.OrderTotal judged to be a CDE while PhoneNumber was not?
options: OrderTotal is financially material, drives real decisions, and has substantial downstream reach, while PhoneNumber meets none of those strongly
OrderTotal has more characters in its column name
PhoneNumber is a CDE and OrderTotal is not
Both columns were judged to be CDEs
questions.explain: OrderTotal feeds revenue recognition, fulfillment decisions, and commission calculations; PhoneNumber doesn't meet the regulatory, financial, decision-impact, or downstream-reach criteria strongly.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which regulatory framework explicitly requires banks to identify and govern their critical data elements?
options: BCBS 239
ISO/IEC 11179
The business glossary approval workflow from Lesson 8
INFORMATION_SCHEMA
questions.explain: BCBS 239 is a banking regulatory framework that explicitly drove the CDE concept's origin, though the underlying idea generalizes well beyond regulated industries.
